note: Which workflow step each test suite guards -- the grouping of the dev server's /test-gate page.
It is a READING AID, never a selection: which suites run is decided by the changed paths
(gate-lib.ps1's Get-AffectedSuiteSelection locally; on CI every suite, except on a PR that
changes only static assets, #3309), never by the group a suite is in; a merge or fold push to
main skips them all or none. A group
says what breaks when its suites go red, not when they run.
Every *.tests.ps1 here is in exactly one group, in workflow order, and dev-pages.tests.ps1 holds
the file to that: a new suite goes into the group whose step it guards, in the same PR.

groups.title: Starting and parking a branch
groups.guards: claim-issue, new-branch, worktree-lane and the parking that keeps a branch on origin until it has a PR
tips: The new-branch suites build a throwaway git repo for each scenario, which is why this is one of the heaviest groups.
Run one suite alone with powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/<name>.tests.ps1 before suspecting the whole gate.
groups.split: new-branch on its own (its three suites carry most of the time), the parking (park-branch, park-commit, park-cycle), and claiming and worktree lanes.

groups.title: Opening, shipping and merging a PR
groups.guards: open-pr and ship-pr: the branch-entry gate, the PR body, the resolves gate, the gate evidence and the merge
tips: open-pr runs locally only the suites the branch's changes can affect, plus every suite that walks the live tree, and leaves the whole pool to the required CI check; -AllSuites runs every one (#3223).
ship-pr may skip its local re-run when CI has already certified the same commit.

groups.title: After the merge: the fold
groups.guards: fold-changelog-entry and the CI runners that fold and verify the resolved issues after a merge
tips: The code these suites guard runs after the merge, on main, where no PR gate stands in front of it. A red here is worth reading closely.

groups.title: The release cut
groups.guards: cut-release and the release documents: the version bump, the tag, the release notes and the reach of each entry
tips: cut-release-drive drives the real cut-release.ps1 against a throwaway repo; it never bumps or tags this one.

groups.title: The lint gate
groups.guards: check-plugin-integrity and the sync checks open-pr runs before the suites: links, roster, manifests, shared scripts, the always-on budget
tips: These suites test the lint; the lint itself runs in its own CI job. A red check-plugin-integrity-* suite means a check changed, not that the tree broke it.
This is the heaviest group, about a third of the sum.
groups.split: check-plugin-integrity on its own (its 15 suites), and the other gates beside it: the always-on budget, the roster, the script contract, the shared scripts, the house style and its palette, mojibake and parameter binding.

groups.title: CI and the test gate itself
groups.guards: the CI workflows, the shards, the suite runner and its fixtures, and the scheduled checks on the repo's settings and stranded PRs
tips: A suite red under the gate and green alone is evidence about the run first: re-run it alone before hunting the failure.
Durations come from CI logs via scripts/maintenance/record-suite-durations.ps1, never from a workstation.
groups.split: the suite runner and its fixtures (test-suite-gate, ci-shard, suite-durations-lib, the three fixture libs), and the CI workflows with their scheduled checks (workflow-concurrency, workflow-timeouts, merge-queue-prereq, ci-merge-skip-lib, ci-suite-selection-lib, repo-settings, stranded and unshipped PRs).

groups.title: Session hooks and the close-out
groups.guards: what runs without anyone asking: the SessionStart checks, the PreToolUse guards, the Stop hooks and the close-out receipt
tips: A session runs the installed plugin copy, not this tree, so a hook change reaches a session here only after a release.
groups.split: the SessionStart checks (claude-home, connector, consumer-prose, git-identity, release-freshness); the tool-use guards (command-guard-lib, guard-working-copy, background-run-lib, hook-fail-closed); the Stop hooks and the close-out (cycle-autopark, closeout-gate, closeout-lib); and the hook plumbing (hook-check-lib, hook-stdin-guard, session-cache-lib).

groups.title: Adoption in a consumer repo
groups.guards: what a consuming repo installs: the adopt skills, the bootstrap and teardown, the config blueprint and the templates it is handed
tips: What these suites guard reaches a consumer by two channels: plugin code after a release, the CI runners scaffolded into it at once, since they track main.

groups.title: Machine upkeep and measuring
groups.guards: the tools a session runs on request: tidy-machine, prune-merged, the plugin updates, the connector and sibling checks, and the measure skills
tips: Most of these run only when somebody asks for them, so a regression here goes unnoticed in daily work until the suite catches it.
groups.split: the measure skills (measure-always-on, measure-session-start, measure-skill, closeout-measure); machine upkeep (tidy-lib, prune-merged, plugin-versions, update-plugins); and the cross-repo checks (connectors, the sibling checks, policy-drift, find-specialist-mentions, fanout).

groups.title: The dev server pages
groups.guards: the hub and its pages, the server that serves them, the hook that starts it and the live issue dashboard
tips: The hub restarts itself when HEAD moves, so a commit shows on the page within seconds; a page that looks stale is usually mid-restart.

groups.title: The BWJ extension
groups.guards: bwj-development: its hooks, the market URLs, the pages worker and the shared test harness it ships
tips: bwj-development is not enabled in this repo, but its suites still run on every PR here, because this repo is its source.

groups.title: The Shopify team
groups.guards: dkj-subagents-shopify: the pre-task sync, the live-theme guard and backups, theme pushes and the live-push rules
tips: dkj-subagents-shopify is not enabled in this repo, but its suites still run on every PR here, because this repo is its source.

groups.title: Shared building blocks
groups.guards: the libs nearly every script loads: console output and escaping, git and native-command capture, the repo root and config, the seams
tips: native-capture-lib.ps1 also ships as plugin mirrors in dkj-policy and dkj-subagents-shopify; change the copy in scripts/lib and keep the mirrors identical.
groups.split: console output and escaping (check-report-lib, ref-print-lib, the exception and wording guards, run-progress); git and native-command capture (git-porcelain-lib, native-capture, fetch-attempt, command-probe-lib); and the repo root, config and seams (repo-config, repo-root-lib, seam-lib, source-repo-guard and the consumer libs).
